question: What is the term used to describe programs that distinguish between uppercase and lowercase letters, treating "yes" and "YES" as different inputs?
solution:
The correct answer is __Case-sensitive.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Case-sensitive__ programs differentiate between uppercase and lowercase letters.
 
• They treat inputs like "yes" and "YES" as distinct values.
 
• Case-sensitive systems are commonly found in passwords and programming languages.
 
• It is crucial to maintain the correct case to ensure proper functionality.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Case-insensitive:**

 
 
• Case-insensitive systems treat uppercase and lowercase letters as equivalent.
 
• For example, inputs like "yes" and "YES" are interpreted as the same.
 
 
 
• **Applications:**
 
 
• Case-sensitive programming is widely used in Linux and Unix environments.
 
• Case-insensitive systems are more common in Windows-based applications.
